title: Base change for the dualizing object of a projection
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension
$d$, put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta=(\operatorname{id}_X,\operatorname{id}_X):X\to W$. The square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W& \xrightarrow{\ p_2\ }&X\\
p_1\big\downarrow &&\big\downarrow f\\
X&\xrightarrow{\ f\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian and $p_1$ is smooth (the base change of $f$); by the
base-change theorem [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] (the comparison of
[def-pur-co-smoothness]),

$$
\omega_{p_1}=Rp_1^!\Lambda_X
\;\cong\;Lp_2^*Rf^!\Lambda_Y=Lp_2^*\omega_f,
$$

and symmetrically $\omega_{p_2}\cong Lp_1^*\omega_f$. Here $C$ denotes the section invariant of [def-pur-section-invariant]. In
particular, since $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$,

$$
C(p_1,\Delta)=L\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}
\;\cong\;L\Delta^*Lp_2^*\omega_f
\;\cong\;\omega_f.
$$

proof.text: Work with the existing coefficient quotient A = O_E/(varpi^n) and its universe lift. The spectral absolute value of ell in E is the p-adic norm of ell, which is less than one. Thus ell belongs to the maximal ideal m_E. The recorded uniformizer generates m_E, so ell^n belongs to (varpi)^n and its image in A is zero. This uses the membership and generator assertions of the recorded DVR theorem; it requires no condition that the ramification index divide n. The integer ell^n is positive because ell is prime. The local-unit assertion coefficientPrime_isUnit_stalk makes its image a unit in every stalk of X, since X is a scheme over the fixed field and ell differs from the characteristic. The stalkwise unit criterion makes it a unit in global sections, giving HasInvertibleExponent A X. Finiteness of A is the existing finiteComparedCoefficientFinite instance.

source.place: Finite coefficient conventions; the recorded DVR theorem and the existing coefficientPrime_isUnit_stalk supply the membership, generator and local-unit assertions.

proof.text: The structure morphism aY is locally of finite type over the spectrum of a field, so LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian gives that Y is locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated. The self-product has its canonical Cartesian square and the flipped square. Both projections are smooth of relative dimension d by base-change stability. Their compactifications come from base change of the given compactification of f, and they are quasi-compact by base-change stability. Use the given structure map aX directly for the coefficient-unit assertion; no substitution along hf is necessary.

source.place: The Cartesian self-product specialization; Mathlib Noetherian and smooth/base-change permanence interfaces.

proof.text: Apply the existing canonical smooth exceptional-base-change theorem directly to f and each of the two Cartesian self-product squares. Its source-exponent hypothesis is Step 1 and its quasi-separated-base hypothesis is Step 2. It makes rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap invertible. The dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap is its component at the coefficient unit, followed by the exceptional image of the canonical pullback-unit isomorphism. The lemma isIso_dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap_iff therefore proves invertibility of each specified dualizing map. This uses the underlying smooth base-change result directly instead of importing the entire tensor/invertibility/composition theorem thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness.

source.place: First sentence, base-change clause, specialized with Y prime = X and g = f; upstream SmoothDuality/SmoothBaseChange and UpperShriekCanonicalMaps supply exactly these canonical maps.

proof.text: Keep finiteDiagonalRestriction and diagonalComparedRestriction unchanged: apply the diagonal pullback to the inverse of the first specified base-change isomorphism, then apply leftDerivedUpperStarCompSectionIso at the dualizing object. This existing etale library comparison is the composition comparison followed by identity pullback, using diagonal_snd. Keep diagonalComparedProEtale unchanged as well: comparedSectionPresentation identifies the actual pro-etale section invariant with this etale presentation, and comparison inverse image transports the specified chain. Thus the same diagonal, composition and identity route is retained without the separate constant-ring composition, general ringed-module composition or general ringed-module identity statements.

lean.statement: theorem comparedDiagonalBaseChange (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] (aX : X ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aX] [QuasiCompact aX] (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY] (hf : f ≫ aY = aX) : IsPullback (pullback.snd f f) (pullback.fst f f) f f ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (pullback.fst f f) ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (pullback.snd f f) ∧ IsIso (Etale.dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap P.Coefficient (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f f).flip) ∧ IsIso (Etale.dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap P.Coefficient (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f f))
